summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with chronic pancreatitis likely due to underlying vasculitis, was readmitted for recurrent abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting just three days after a prior discharge. She had not tolerated oral prednisone, which exacerbated her nausea. During this admission, she was managed supportively with NPO status, IV fluids, and IV Dilaudid for pain. Her PPI was switched to IV famotidine due to an allergy to IV pantoprazole, and prednisone was discontinued. Her symptoms improved over 72 hours, she advanced to a regular diet, and her medications were transitioned back to oral form. A urine culture suggested possible contamination, but a short course of Macrobid was prescribed as a precaution. She received parenteral nutrition before discharge. The patient was discharged home in good condition, with pain controlled and oral intake tolerated, and instructed to follow up with her specialist to address long-term management of her vasculitis and prevent recurrent admissions.
